text: On a damp March morning at Varnholt Logistics’ riverfront headquarters, the board named Ilse Marrenkamp chief executive, ending a six-month interim period and signaling a steadier course for the century-old freight group. Marrenkamp, 52, had spent most of her career in cross-border warehousing and rail coordination, most recently as operations director at the company’s Graden branch. Her appointment follows a difficult winter of delayed shipments, rising fuel costs and a bruising audit that prompted the departure of her predecessor, Tomas Vehr. Founded in 1919 as a family haulier, Varnholt has grown into one of Northfold’s largest private employers, with 4,800 staff across nine depots. Board chair Selma Draak said Marrenkamp was chosen for “calm judgment and practical repair.”
